correctness.rationale: The graph is explicitly specified for every \(r\ge1\). Every local fort of \(K_6-M_3\) is classified; hub-free global minimal forts are supported on exactly one block. Hub-containing fort status is equivalent to local domination in all blocks, which forces at least two vertices per block; minimality forces exactly two nonmate vertices per block. Both necessity and sufficiency are proved against arbitrary proper subforts. This disjoint exhaustive classification gives \(3r\), \(8r\), \(12^r\) terms; for \(r=1\) the coincident size-three terms sum. The limit follows from order \(6r+1\). Independently exhaustive all-subset computation for \(r=1\),2,3 matches profiles (532605 total nonempty candidate subsets) but is not used as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The relevant complete 2024 primary paper gives the general fort framework and clique-page windmills, explicitly credits the \(3^{1/3}\) record and asks for stronger graph families; it does not give the asserted \(K_6-M_3\) bouquet family or its full polynomial. The old \(K_{2,2,2}\) result determines page-local minimal forts, not the assembled graph polynomial or improved rate. The exact new construction improves the previous rate by a strict inequality. Relevant limitations of indexed searches and the potential of an unindexed equivalent construction are stated.
residual_risks: Published or unindexed equivalent construction of \(K_1\) joined to disjoint \(K_{2,2,2}\) pages might exist under generalized friendship, bouquet, windmill, or zero-forcing terminology.
The graph sequence \(B_r\) advances the per-vertex root threshold but does not itself establish the literal consecutive-order ratio limit in the 2024 conjecture.
A related 2025–2026 paper on trees was inspected at abstract level only; it is not considered dispositive for non-tree bouquets.
Finite test cases cannot certify the infinitely quantified theorem without its proof.

value.rationale: Provides a concrete, naturally formulated, connected graph family whose exact minimal-fort count grows at per-vertex base \(12^{1/6}\), strictly exceeding the 2024 windmill benchmark \(3^{1/3}\) in the authors' explicitly conjectured research direction. The full size-generating polynomial and minimality classification are structural and prove more than isolated data, without claiming universal optimality or the conjecture's literal consecutive-order limit.
